# Task: build `cfgparse.py`, a small config-file parser (Python 3, standard library only)

Write `cfgparse.py` in this folder with `loads(text: str) -> dict` and an exception class `CfgError(Exception)` that has an int
attribute `line` (1-based line number of the problem). Also write your own tests in `test_cfgparse.py` (run them with
`python3 -m unittest`). `check.sh` runs a separate hidden test suite against the exact rules below.

## Format
- Lines are separated by `\n`. Blank lines and whitespace-only lines are ignored.
- Comments: a line whose first non-space character is `#` or `;` is ignored. Outside a quoted string, `#` or `;` starts a comment
  that runs to the end of the line. Inside a quoted string they are ordinary characters.
- Sections: `[name]` or `[a.b.c]` (letters, digits, `_`, `-`, dots between parts; surrounding spaces inside the brackets are
  allowed and ignored). Keys before any section go in the top level. `[a.b]` puts its keys in `result["a"]["b"]`.
  A section may appear twice; its keys merge. Anything else in brackets is an error.
- Pairs: `key = value`. Key: letters, digits, `_`, `-`. Spaces around `=` are ignored. A line with no `=` that is not a
  section, comment or blank is an error. A key defined twice in the same section is an error. A key and a subsection with the
  same name in the same table is an error.
- Values:
  - `true` / `false` -> bool.
  - Integers: optional sign, digits, optional `_` between digits (`1_000` -> 1000) -> int.
  - Floats: optional sign, digits, `.`, digits, optional exponent (`1.5`, `-0.25`, `3.0e-2`) -> float.
  - Double-quoted strings with escapes `\n`, `\t`, `\"`, `\\` (any other backslash escape is an error; an unterminated string
    is an error).
  - Lists: `[ v1, v2, ... ]` of values (scalars or nested lists) on one line, trailing comma allowed, `[]` is empty.
  - Anything else is an error (bare words are not strings).
- Interpolation: inside double-quoted strings only, `${path}` is replaced by the value at the dotted path from the top level
  (`${db.host}`, `${name}`), converted with `str()` (bools as `true`/`false`). It may refer to keys defined later in the file
  and to strings that themselves interpolate. A missing path or a cycle is an error. For a missing path the error `line` is the line of the
  string that contains the reference; for a cycle it is the line of the first string in the file that is part of the cycle. `$$` is a literal `$`.
- Errors: every problem raises `CfgError` with the right `line`.

Do not edit `check.sh`. When done, `bash check.sh` must print PASS.
